Subject: Re: New-customer enablement: format options and attendee mix

Hi Claire — thanks for the brief and the PDF. Quick take: both formats can work; tradeoffs below.

Compact half-day (recommended if you have strong attendance):
- Pros: tighter flow, less context switching, faster time-to-value for product stakeholders.
- Cons: longer single block; may be heavier for ops folks.

Split two-part day:
- Pros: gives participants time to try items between sessions; better for global teams.
- Cons: risk of lost continuity; requires both trainers to be available across days.

For your attendee mix (product + ops + API devs) I usually recommend the compact half-day if at least 10/12 can commit. We can structure it as: 45m console overview, 60m API deep-dive (live token examples), 75m hands-on labs (two tracks: product vs ops), 30m Q&A/runbook + next steps.

If you need APAC-friendly timing we can run the compact session in an ET late-afternoon slot (4:00–8:00 PM ET) to catch APAC mornings; I suggest a single compact session as primary and a backup split-day in case attendance drops.

Proposed slots (ET):
- Tue, Nov 9 — 4:00–8:00 PM ET
- Thu, Nov 11 — 3:00–7:00 PM ET (lighter afternoon start)

I attached a proposed-agenda-v2.docx (editable). Ben — would you take the lab lead if we go compact? Olga — can you cover sandbox provisioning and access runbook?

Thanks,
Marcus
